samples.summary: Dropping `href` from CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE leaves an empty-inline href residue unclearable by any command
samples.evidence: `link-run.ts:27-31` documents that `normalizeInlines` leaves an `href` residue on a fully-emptied paragraph, and `findLinkRunAt` deliberately refuses to anchor on an empty-text inline (`inlines[i].text.length > 0` at link-run.ts:44). `removeLink` (editor.ts:3724, text-box-editor.ts:1237) is built on `findLinkRunAt`, so it no-ops on such a run. Until this change, Clear formatting was the one command that stripped that stale `href`; with `href` removed from `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` neither command touches it. Worse, on a collapsed caret in that paragraph `applyStyleImpl` (editor.ts:1170) stores `{ ...caretInlineStyle(...), ...CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE }`, and `caretInlineStyle` has no residue guard (caret-style.ts:106-112), so the pending style now carries the residual `href` and the next typed characters become a hyperlink the user never created. `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` cannot help: an empty run fails its `position.offset > start` test.

samples.summary: Stale-pending fallback `prev.href === undefined` ignores the pending anchor, so a link exit can be re-armed at an unrelated caret
samples.evidence: `pending.get()` (pending-style.ts:20) returns the style with no anchor check, and `PendingStyle` state survives a caret move made through `EditorAPI.restoreLocalCursor` (editor.ts:4338-4352 never calls `pending.clear()`), which the collaboration layer runs on every remote change. If an exit was armed earlier (`exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge`) and the caret subsequently lands *inside* a link without a mousedown/arrow (both of which do clear pending), `exitsLink` is true from the stale `prev` alone and Clear formatting arms `href: undefined` — the next typed character drops the link the change is supposed to preserve. Same code in editor.ts:3367. Comparing the pending anchor against `cursor.position` would close it.

samples.summary: Only the trailing edge is guarded: at the *leading* edge of a link the toolbar clear seeds pending with the link's href and extends the link backwards
samples.evidence: `caretInlineStyle` returns the first run whose end >= offset (caret-style.ts:106-112), so at offset 0 of a block whose first run is a link the caret style carries that `href`. `applyStyleImpl`'s collapsed branch stores `{ ...caretStyle, ...CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE }` (editor.ts:1170) and `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` no longer has an `href` key, so Clear formatting there re-arms the link and the next typed character joins it — the exact failure the trailing-edge override was added to prevent, at the opposite edge. `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` only tests `position.offset === end`, never the leading boundary.

samples.summary: New Remove-link button only drops the one link run at the caret, so a multi-link selection silently keeps its other links now that Clear formatting preserves hrefs
samples.evidence: `handleRemoveLink` calls `editor.removeLink?.()`, which in both implementations (editor.ts:3719-3737, text-box-editor.ts:1234-1248) resolves a single run via `findLinkRunAt(block, cursor.position.offset)` and applies `{ href: undefined }` to just that run — the current selection is ignored entirely. Before this change, Clear formatting over a selection removed every `href` in it; that path is now deliberately gone, so a user who selects a paragraph containing several links and clicks Remove link gets at most one of them removed (and none at all when the caret happens to sit outside a link), with no feedback.

samples.summary: `EditorAPI.removeLink` throws instead of no-opping on a stale caret block — the `if (!block) return` guard is dead
samples.evidence: `doc.getBlock` throws `Block not found` when the id is unknown (document.ts:202-216), so `const block = doc.getBlock(cursor.position.blockId); if (!block) return;` can never take the guard and instead propagates an exception. This is now the command the change designates as the *only* way to drop a hyperlink (types.ts:300 comment, editor.ts:99), and the new toolbar wiring pattern calls `removeLink()` unconditionally without any try/catch (`text-format-group.tsx:174-178`), so a caret pointing at a block a collaborator just deleted turns a toolbar click into an uncaught error. The slides path is safe because `text-box-editor.ts:1235` uses `findBlock`; the docs path is not.

finding.summary: Dropping `href` from CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE leaves an empty-inline href residue unclearable by any command
finding.evidence: `link-run.ts:27-31` documents that `normalizeInlines` leaves an `href` residue on a fully-emptied paragraph, and `findLinkRunAt` deliberately refuses to anchor on an empty-text inline (`inlines[i].text.length > 0` at link-run.ts:44). `removeLink` (editor.ts:3724, text-box-editor.ts:1237) is built on `findLinkRunAt`, so it no-ops on such a run. Until this change, Clear formatting was the one command that stripped that stale `href`; with `href` removed from `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` neither command touches it. Worse, on a collapsed caret in that paragraph `applyStyleImpl` (editor.ts:1170) stores `{ ...caretInlineStyle(...), ...CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE }`, and `caretInlineStyle` has no residue guard (caret-style.ts:106-112), so the pending style now carries the residual `href` and the next typed characters become a hyperlink the user never created. `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` cannot help: an empty run fails its `position.offset > start` test.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the repo. `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` (model/types.ts:300-315) no longer contains `href`. The empty-text `href` residue is real and editor-reachable: normalizeInlines (store/block-helpers.ts:105-111) preserves the emptied run's style and deletes only `image`, and test/view/edit-link-in-place.test.ts:245-253 produces it via insertLink+backspace. `findLinkRunAt` refuses to anchor on it (view/link-run.ts:44, documented 26-32), and `removeLink` early-returns on that undefined (view/editor.ts:3724-3725), so Remove Hyperlink no-ops. The new `exitsLink` override cannot save it: isAtLinkTrailingEdge requires `position.offset > start` (model/caret-style.ts:80), which is `0 > 0` for a zero-length inline, so editor.ts:3364-3372 and text-editor.ts:3440-3446 take the plain CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE branch. applyStyleImpl then stores `{ ...caretInlineStyle(...), ...CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE }` (editor.ts:1170) and caretInlineStyle returns `{ ...defaults, ...inline.style }` with no residue guard (caret-style.ts:106-110), so the pending style carries href; consumeForInsert applies it verbatim to the typed range (view/pending-style.ts:34-40). I searched the typing path for a compensating guard (docInsertText text-editor.ts:628-633, applyInsertText block-helpers.ts:117-146) and found none, so no `already-guarded` refutation is available. The reviewer slightly overstates causation — the residue makes typed text a link even without invoking Clear formatting — but the defect (an href state no command can clear, yielding a hyperlink the user never created) is real and reachable in normal use, which keeps it in the correctness lane.

finding.summary: New link-trailing-edge guard is bolted onto `clearInlineFormatting` only; every other caller of `applyStyleImpl`'s collapsed-caret branch still re-arms the link from the caret style
finding.evidence: `applyStyleImpl` (editor.ts:1170) stores `pending.set({ ...getSelectionStyleImpl(), ...style }, cursor.position)`. `getSelectionStyleImpl()` is the raw caret style, which at a link's trailing edge is the link run's style **including `href`**, and the prior pending state is NOT merged in — so any pending `href: undefined` armed by `exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge` is discarded. The diff patches only the `clearInlineFormatting` entry (editor.ts:3364-3372). The bypassing call sites are `applyStyle: applyStyleImpl` (editor.ts:3342 — toolbar Bold/Italic/color/etc.) and `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl`'s collapsed branch (editor.ts:1283). Concretely: click the caret at the end of a hyperlink (mousedown clears pending), click toolbar Bold, type a character — the pending style carries the link's `href`, so `consumeForInsert` writes it onto the new text and the hyperlink silently grows. That is exactly the failure mode the new override exists to prevent, reachable through the sibling toolbar buttons. (Pre-existing shape, but it is the path around the new guard.)

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present as described. applyStyleImpl's collapsed branch stages `{ ...getSelectionStyleImpl(), ...style }` (editor.ts:1170), where getSelectionStyleImpl returns the raw caret run style (caret-style.ts:106-114) — which at a link's trailing edge includes `href` (caret-style.ts:61-68) — and PendingStyle.set replaces rather than merges (pending-style.ts:22-24), so any armed `href: undefined` is discarded. The new trailing-edge override is only on the clearInlineFormatting entry (editor.ts:3362-3372); the sibling call sites `applyStyle: applyStyleImpl` (editor.ts:3342) and stepSelectionFontSizeImpl's collapsed branch (editor.ts:1283) reach the same staging with no such override — and stepSelectionFontSize even reads pending (1279-1281) only to discard it. The path is concretely reachable and diverges from baseline: exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge arms `href: undefined` (text-editor.ts:5912-5917) and survives an Enter split via rebindAnchor (text-editor.ts:655-659, 2641-2642), while the new empty block inherits the link's style including href through getSplitPointStyle (block-helpers.ts:228-232, used at :275-277). Clicking toolbar Bold after that Enter re-arms href, and consumeForInsert then writes it onto the typed text (pending-style.ts:28-42 via docInsertText, text-editor.ts:628-633). Ordinary character input never re-runs the exit (only space :977-982, Enter :2608/:2641, paste :4171), so nothing corrects it — the hyperlink silently grows. Note the keyboard path toggleStyle does merge pending (text-editor.ts:3465-3468), confirming the merge is the intended contract. Wrong behavior on a normal-use path in the correctness lane; no guard or caller makes it unreachable.
